records.title: Dispatch Loom
records.subtitle: Dispatch reconciliation tool
records.summary: Personally designed and built an operational dispatch reconciliation tool using Python and SQL. It reconciled mismatched dispatch references, with operators comparing an overnight spreadsheet against a daily export. Personally wrote the Python parser and SQL checks; used Git for version control and PostgreSQL for production data. The team result was reduced reconciliation time, not measured delivery speed. The supervisors made final dispatch decisions.

decisions.reason: The name, role description, and all listed denials are supported by the source.

The employer, dates, project contributions, supervisor interactions, tools, training, and linked outcomes are supported in the employment context. The record does not assert a disputed workshop headcount.
The project description, aliases, workflow, personal contributions, team context, tools, and stated limitations are supported by the source and its clarifications.
The separate SQL checklist, personal construction, night-shift handover documentation, and absence of a recorded user count or measured outcome are supported.
The training and handbook details are supported, but attendance is explicitly unresolved: recollection says 12 and a later sheet says 14.
The 5-to-2-hour weekly reconciliation result over six runs, its team attribution, the 3-hour calculation, Ada's stated contribution, and the delivery-speed clarification are supported.
The personal Roster Note handover documentation and absence of a claimed measured impact are supported.
The source supports Python use for Dispatch Loom and Ada's personal authorship of its parser.
The source supports SQL use for Dispatch Loom checks, extensive SQL use, and the SQL Roster Note checklist.
The source identifies PostgreSQL as the production database; context clarifies this was part of the same Dispatch Loom work.
The source identifies Git for version control and clarifies that it held changes for the same work.
Coworker training and the two workshops are supported, but the record also includes an explicitly unresolved attendance figure: 12 by recollection or 14 on a later sheet.
